newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end firmer in very quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end firmer in very quiet trading.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Friday, helped by gains in U.S. treasuries, with activity very light ahead of what will be a holiday weekend for many traders, analysts said.

"One out of 10 customers is here this afternoon, so I'm not sure this is very meaningful," said one bond trader with a bank-owned brokerage. "I wouldn't describe the closing prices as being very meaningful. The market's illiquid.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.36 to C$115.29 to yield 6.797 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 14/32 to yield 6.75 percent. The spread between the bonds was five basis points, unchanged from Thursday's close.
Canadian bond prices tumbled on Thursday after the Bank of Canada surprised the market by raising its key bank rate by 25 basis points to 3.5 percent, it's first rate hike in more than two years.
While bonds initally weakened on the hike, analysts said the long end of the curve benefited today from the belief that the move would help control inflation in the long term.
"The Bank of Canada's move, if anything, calmed any types of fears about future inflation, warranted or not," said Marcel Kasumovich, an economist with Goldman Sachs Canada.
Today's session was quiet with many traders taking holidays ahead of the Canada Day holiday next Tuesday.
The approaching meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Open Market Committee beginning on July 1, and the approach of quarter end also kept activity light.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.25 to C$107.40 to yield 6.237 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which rose 8/32 to yield 6.46 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 22 basis points from 23 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.16 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.14 percent.
